title: Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on the Judiciary, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Sectoral AI Governance Act of 2026 establishes tailored regulations and oversight for artificial intelligence in key industries such as healthcare, finance, and transportation. It aims to ensure AI systems in these sectors are safe, transparent, and aligned with public interests, while encouraging responsible innovation.

title: Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Stop AI Price Gouging and Wage Fixing Act of 2025 aims to prevent AI companies from charging excessively high prices for their services and from manipulating wages in the AI industry. It proposes regulatory measures to enforce fair pricing and wage practices, protecting both consumers and workers from exploitative AI-driven markets.

title: American AI Security Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select), for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The American AI Security Act is a U.S. law aimed at protecting national security by setting standards and oversight for artificial intelligence systems. It establishes regulations that require AI developers and users to meet safety, transparency, and accountability requirements to prevent misuse and ensure the technology benefits society.

title: Expressing the sense of the House of Representatives that Congress must refuse to provide any additional funds or exceptional regulatory support to companies or financial institutions facing insolvency or financial collapse due to exposures to acute stress within the artificial intelligence market and must provide support to all harmed Americans instead.
action: Referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committees on the Judiciary, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The House of Representatives says Congress should not give more money or special regulatory help to companies or financial institutions at risk of collapse because of stress in the AI market. Instead, it urges Congress to provide support to all Americans who have been harmed.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a regulatory framework that governs the use of AI in vocational education and training. It sets rules to ensure AI tools used in training are safe, transparent, and respect learners’ rights.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 bars the use of AI systems for diagnosing or treating patients, requiring that all medical care be performed by licensed doctors. This measure is intended to protect patients by ensuring human oversight and accountability in healthcare.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 requires companies that build and use automated decision‑making systems to assess their algorithms for bias, safety, and other risks. It also mandates that these companies disclose how their algorithms work and provide a way for regulators and consumers to review and challenge the decisions those systems make.

title: Securing Elections From AI Deception Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Securing Elections From AI Deception Act seeks to protect the integrity of elections by addressing risks from artificial intelligence systems that could spread misinformation or manipulate voters. It proposes stricter transparency requirements for AI‑generated content, safeguards for election communication channels, and enforcement measures to hold developers and users accountable for deceptive AI practices.

title: Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The Reliable Artificial Intelligence Research Act of 2026 establishes a legal framework to ensure AI research is conducted safely, transparently, and with accountability, setting standards for reliability, testing, and documentation. It also creates oversight mechanisms, funding incentives, and collaboration agreements to promote responsible development and deployment of AI technologies.

title: VA AI Transparency Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA AI Transparency Act of 2026 requires the Department of Veterans Affairs to disclose how AI systems are used in its operations, ensuring veterans and the public understand the decision‑making processes behind AI‑driven tools. The Act mandates regular audits, reporting standards, and public access to documentation so that the impact of AI on veterans’ services is clear, accountable, and compliant with privacy and ethical guidelines.

title: VA Claims AI Accountability Act
action: Referred to the Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations.
summary: The VA Claims AI Accountability Act seeks to regulate the use of artificial intelligence in processing veterans' claims, ensuring that AI systems are transparent, fair, and accountable. It aims to protect veterans by establishing clear guidelines and oversight for AI-driven decision-making in benefits determination.

title: Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute (Amended) by the Yeas and Nays: 35 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Consumers from Deceptive AI Act is a policy aimed at safeguarding consumers from misleading or deceptive AI technologies. It establishes guidelines and enforcement mechanisms to ensure transparency, accountability, and consumer protection in AI applications.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is intended to strengthen the security of advanced artificial intelligence systems by setting national standards and guidelines for development, deployment, and monitoring. It also encourages collaboration between government, academia, and industry to identify and mitigate potential threats, ensuring AI technology is both reliable and resilient.

title: CISA Securing AI Task Force Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Homeland Security.
summary: The CISA Securing AI Task Force Act establishes a federal task force to protect the nation’s AI systems from cyber threats. It aims to coordinate efforts across government agencies, develop security standards, share threat intelligence, and build resilience against AI‑related attacks.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Management and Security Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to protect people and society from the potential dangers of advanced AI systems. It sets rules and standards for how companies develop, test, and use AI, ensuring they keep safety, transparency, and accountability in mind.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This Act establishes guidelines for designing, deploying, and overseeing AI-powered physical systems to ensure they are safe, reliable, and meet national standards. It also promotes coordination among manufacturers, regulators, and users to share best practices and mitigate potential risks.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: This act seeks to safeguard elections by preventing deceptive AI systems from influencing voters and spreading misinformation. It sets out rules and penalties to promote transparency, accountability, and the integrity of the electoral process.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act is a policy aimed at ensuring that AI systems that can modify themselves are closely watched for safety and compliance. It establishes requirements for continuous oversight, reporting, and accountability measures so that any unintended or harmful behavior can be detected and addressed promptly.

title: Stop Rogue AI Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The "Stop Rogue AI Act" is a proposed law designed to curb the risk of harmful or unauthorized AI behavior by setting strict safety and accountability standards for developers. It requires AI systems to have built‑in safeguards, transparent operation logs, and enforceable penalties to prevent autonomous actions that could threaten public safety.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act proposes a pause on the construction and operation of new large-scale data centers that power AI systems. It aims to curb the environmental impact of these facilities while encouraging the development of greener, more sustainable AI infrastructure.

title: Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Cybersecurity and AI Board of Investigations Act of 2026 establishes a federal board to oversee and investigate cybersecurity incidents involving artificial intelligence systems, ensuring they meet national security and safety standards. The act requires organizations to report AI‑related breaches, imposes compliance requirements, and coordinates responses to protect public safety and national interests.

title: Make AI Work for Americans Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Finance.
summary: The Make AI Work for Americans Act is a proposed law aimed at ensuring that the development and use of artificial‑intelligence technologies benefit the U.S. public. It seeks to promote transparency, accountability, and safeguards so that AI tools are created and deployed in ways that advance national interests, protect privacy, and avoid harmful or unfair impacts.
